results.ask: What's special about my block? I'm on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega.
results.expect: calls about_block; gives the block's own figures and something pinned nearby, with sources; cites
results.answer:
Your block sits about 39 feet above sea level and its homes were mostly built around 1941. Two model homes from World War II stood a few doors east: Doelger's Rainbow House (1941) and Freedom House (1942) on 42nd and 43rd Avenues between Moraga and Noriega.

Nearby, the Noriega seawall (1980s) catches windblown sand every year, and the buried hull of the clipper ship King Philip (1878) lies under the sand near Noriega and Ortega.

Old photographs of your corner are on OpenSFHistory: [wnp58.929](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.929.jpg) and [wnp58.923](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.923.jpg).

Street cleaning is:
- East side: Mondays 1st & 3rd, noon–2pm (next 11/16)
- West side: Thursdays 1st, 3rd, 5th, noon–2pm (next 11/19)

The signs on the block are the last word.

A neighbor who watched the block change over the years could tell you more.
